event: Drought and agricultural stress preceding the 2011 uprising
social_impact: Agricultural livelihood losses; proposed migration and grievance pathways
conflict_relationship: Contribution to conflict onset is disputed; no single-cause explanation established
climate_attribution: Attribution of drought to climate change is separate from attribution of war to drought
limitations: Do not label the Syrian civil war as caused by climate change. Poor water management, agricultural policy and political factors also matter.

social_impact: Pressures on livelihoods and resource access
conflict_relationship: Environmental pressures interacted with exclusion, government policy, weakened conflict-resolution mechanisms and prior violence
climate_attribution: Climate change is not established as the primary cause of the conflict
limitations: Do not label Darfur the first climate war. This case does not establish causes of the separate Sudan war beginning in 2023.

event: Drought interacting with ongoing armed conflict
social_impact: Food and income insecurity; displacement; restricted resource and market access
conflict_relationship: Drought and conflict compound vulnerability; conflict limits adaptation and assistance
climate_attribution: Climate hazards contribute to vulnerability, not an established origin of the war
limitations: Overlapping drought and conflict do not prove that drought caused the war.

event: Water and livelihood stress during conflict
period_label: No single event period specified in preceding summary
social_impact: Agricultural disruption; displacement pressures; local resource disputes
conflict_relationship: Environmental stress and war can reinforce vulnerability and local tensions
climate_attribution: No attribution of national war onset to climate change established here
limitations: Qualitative case, not a quantified effect or proof of national conflict causation; detailed source passage should be checked before public claims.

climate_attribution: Climate change likely increased extreme rainfall; overall contribution could not be precisely quantified
limitations: Movements are not unique people; may include evacuation and repeated displacement. Count is not the number displaced solely by anthropogenic climate change.
indicator: Internal displacement movements triggered by floods

social_impact: Reduced wheat yields; power shortages; dangerous outdoor working conditions
climate_attribution: Attribution study estimated the heatwave was about 30 times more likely due to human-caused warming
limitations: Event-specific estimate; does not mean all heatwaves are 30 times more likely. Multi-country event is one observation, not two independent country estimates.
indicator: Event likelihood relative to a pre-industrial climate

social_impact: Reduced wheat yields; power shortages; dangerous outdoor working conditions
climate_attribution: Attribution study estimated the heatwave was about 1 degree Celsius hotter due to human-caused warming
limitations: Same event as the likelihood record; not an additional disaster or independent population count.
indicator: Additional heatwave intensity due to human-caused warming

hazard: Failed rainy seasons; heat and evaporation
social_impact: Crop failure; livestock deaths; displacement; hunger compounded by conflict
conflict_relationship: Conflict worsened drought vulnerability and constrained response
